html:
The Khait earthquake struck the mountains of central Tajikistan, then a Soviet republic, on 10 July 1949. It had a magnitude of 7.5.

The shaking itself did less harm than what followed. It set off landslides on slopes already soaked by rain and covered in loose dust and soil. A huge flow of earth and mud poured down the valley and buried the town of Khait, along with nearby villages, under deep debris. Around 7,200 people died, most of them in the landslides.

Like other disasters under Soviet rule in these years, such as the Ashgabat earthquake the year before, it was barely reported at the time. It remains one of the deadliest examples of an earthquake causing landslides, much like the Usoi landslide in the Pamirs in 1911.
sum: The Khait earthquake struck the mountains of central Tajikistan, then a Soviet republic, on 10 July 1949. It had a magnitude of 7.5.
